llm.summary: This Windows cleanup skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it includes under-scoped system and file-move powers that users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Broad C drive scanning and user-file movement fit a disk cleanup skill, but arbitrary confirmed paths, Program Files compression, and system cleanup commands are high-impact for a non-technical-user workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains local PowerShell scripts and documentation; I found no hidden installer, package download, network callback, or credential setup.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main instructions emphasize not touching software program directories and only moving safe items, while supporting references and scripts allow broader actions than that framing suggests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill stores a local habit.json-style preference file and describes optional monthly checks; this is disclosed, but scheduling and auto-clean boundaries are not fully specified.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is consent-gated C drive cleanup, but the reference workflow goes beyond relocation and safe cache handling by recommending NTFS compression of Program Files paths and CompactOS/DISM operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a local Windows cleanup helper that can scan C:, move files after confirmation, store cleanup preferences, and potentially guide advanced system cleanup. Before using it, avoid approving Program Files compression, CompactOS/DISM changes, or arbitrary folder moves unless you understand the rollback path and have backups.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: references/workflow.md includes CompactOS and DISM execution steps plus Program Files compression, which exceeds the prominently stated 'only move files' safety model.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: workflow examples run compact.exe against Program Files/Common Files despite the main skill text saying software program directories are not touched.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: scripts/safe_ops.ps1 uses denylist checks and then default-allows unmatched paths for MoveToBackup and SendToRecycle once -Confirmed is supplied.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: the safe_ops.ps1 fallback does not prove an unmatched path is cache/temp data, creating a mismatch with the documented safe-cache-only framing.
[SQP-1] expected: Partly confirmed but downgraded: periodic checks and habit storage are disclosed and default sample autoEnabled is false, though the exact scheduling boundary remains vague.
[SQP-1] expected: Confirmed but limited: promo text uses a common natural-language invocation, which could start a scan unintentionally, but the artifact still requires confirmation before cleanup actions.
